approach: The block m is held up only by friction against the wedge's vertical face, and that friction comes from the normal force created by the sideways acceleration.

steps.text: Since M and m move together, they share one horizontal acceleration.
The wedge pushes block m sideways, so the normal force N between them equals m times that acceleration.
The block has nothing below it, so friction alone must support its weight; for the minimum F, friction is at its maximum value.
Put N = ma into this and solve for a.
steps.equation: μ m a = mg ⇒ a = g/μ
steps.why_this_step: This is the smallest sideways acceleration at which the available friction is exactly enough to hold the block up.

steps.text: Put a = g/μ into the system equation and solve for F.

common_mistakes.text: Leaving block m's own mass out of the accelerating system and writing F = M g / μ instead of (M+m) g / μ.
